resources.string: NFC access cards and HCE status
Keeps NFC on, requests polling mask 0 on discovery and restart, preserves HCE. Verify via runtime logs and hardware tests.
Reader blocking is on. Disable it before scanning a card.
Failed to save NFC reader blocking setting.
Tap a card to view UID, SAK, and ATQA, then start or stop emulation.
No saved cards. Enter read mode, tap a card, verify its information, then save it.
Applying UID %1$s through the NFC process
Disabled. Logs are not collected to reduce performance impact.
Diagnostics are automatically saved under Download/YSuite/YNFC/; live logs remain available below.
Stop emulation before entering read mode.

Emulation is active, so read mode remains disabled.
Read mode is enabled. Hold the access card against the back of the phone.
Cards are not read by default. Enable read mode only when adding a new card.
Card read successfully. Verify the information before saving.
NFC service process not found. Check Android NFC is enabled.

No NFC Hook callback. Enable the com.android.nfc scope for YSuite in LSPosed, then reload the NFC service process if necessary. Root alone does not activate the Hook; a full phone reboot is normally unnecessary.
Hook belongs to an older NFC process. Wait for the new NFC service to load its Hook; no full phone reboot is needed.
NFC process exists, but its LSPosed scope is not confirmed. Verify the com.android.nfc scope, then reload only the NFC service if needed.
YNFC scope reported, but no Hook was installed. Export focused LSPosed logs to see the installation failure.
Installed NFC Hook version differs from the APK. YNFC will try to reload only the NFC service; no full phone reboot is normally needed.
NFC Hook is not ready. Check the scoped process and diagnostic logs.

OFF = strict NFC-A UID replacement via Root/LSPosed RF/NCI (replaces an existing LA_NFCID1, never appends). ON = experimental ColorOS Vendor Type-A, which requires OEM signature/privileged NFC permission. An external reader must verify the actual UID.
Stop the current simulation before changing the backend.
Vendor Type-A request accepted by OEM; actual card emulation has NOT been verified by an external reader.

ColorOS denied Vendor Type-A because the NFC system process lacks com.oplus.permission.safe.NFC (signature|privileged). This cannot be fixed with a normal runtime permission grant. Stop emulation to restore NFC; see diagnostics for details.
No UID was written in the current NFC process. Simulation stopped without restarting NFC; stock RF was not independently verified.

The currently running NFC service has an older injected Hook. APK updates do not require a phone reboot. Reload the NFC service only when you want to activate new Hook code; this briefly interrupts NFC.
Stop UID emulation before reloading the NFC service.
NFC Hook is already current. No reload required.
NFC service reloaded with the updated Hook. Phone reboot not required.
Could not confirm the new NFC Hook. Check LSPosed scope and diagnostic logs; no further restart was attempted.
Only use this after installing a test build with new in-process Hook code. Reloads the NFC service once, not the phone. No automatic restart.
ColorOS rejected native NFC-A disable. Stock RF is not confirmed; check the diagnostic log.

UID replacement not applied: NFC routing refreshed but the current process did not call a usable NCI UID writer. The RF backend only replaces an existing LA_NFCID1; it never appends another parameter. This firmware may require a separate, verified native HAL interception point.
Replace UID/ATQA/SAK only when ColorOS naturally calls HceAccessCard. This mode does not request or force an OEM NFC-A write; external reader verification is required.
ColorOS HCE method used the imported parameters and returned success. The actual RF UID is still unverified; check with an external NFC reader.
No ColorOS Type-A call observed yet. File interception remains armed until you stop it; the UID has not been verified or replaced so far.
Reload NFC service to test interception
NFC service reloaded. Interception remains armed; check for new HCE calls and verify with an external NFC reader.
File interception is not armed. Select Intercept and tap Simulate on a saved card before reloading NFC.
No import required. Tap Simulate on a saved card. The validated JSON is created privately and exported to Download/YSuite/YNFC/; ColorOS HCE remains an experimental compatibility path.
Automatic NFC-A/SN220 file preparation failed. No new simulation command was sent; inspect config-status.txt and the diagnostic log.
NFC service is running older Hook code
Stop any running simulation, then manually reload only the NFC service to activate the latest file interception Hook. No phone reboot is needed.
Legacy RF does not provide an independent native UID writer. Select native NCI investigation to collect firmware evidence.
Uses an automatic private NFC-A profile and the device NXP HAL diagnostic path. Native UID writing is disabled until this firmware ABI and controller support are verified. No ColorOS Wallet needed.

Tap Simulate to copy the active SN220 configuration into Download/YSuite/YNFC/original-SN220.conf, create modified-SN220.conf plus selected-nfc-a.json, and verify their hashes. Native NCI interception is not installed; no UID packet is transmitted.
Native NCI/HAL is not ready: exact firmware libraries and the UID writer ABI must be verified before any controller configuration. No UID was simulated or sent. Export a diagnostic report.
